entrypoints.negative_control: make scenario S=E1   # and the proof pack's OPS-NC

items.text: Admission with a work-in-system bound and an explicit capacity error (128 = slots + queue bound)
Weighted fair scheduling (deficit round robin, 3:1) with a finance bulkhead of 16
Bounded concurrency, deadline-aware dequeue and cooperative cancellation
Workflow resource envelopes and a ledger shared with child workflows
Routing inside an eligibility contract with policy-aware fallback
Bounded retrieval and a cache keyed by tenant, principal scope, knowledge and policy version
A tool gateway: per-tool concurrency, rate limit, bounded priority wait, circuit breaker
Content-addressed release manifests, a registry that refuses ungated releases, an invariant gate and a mix-adjusted canary

classes.meaning: the actual mechanism was exercised: each control is real code, executed on every simulated request

items.text: The clock (integer simulated milliseconds), the model providers (latency, quotas, 429), the downstream APIs (capacity, 503, 429) and the clients (timeouts, retries)
Scripted agents: the plans are fixed per workflow type; the only behaviour a release changes is declared (a tool description, a prompt length, a routing table)
Cost in cost units (cu): synthetic per-1k-token rates, per-query and per-call charges; not any provider's prices
The eligibility contract and the success table by capability gap (config/models.toml): routing is tested within them, never real model quality
Processor-sharing contention beyond 32 concurrent workflows; a downstream that slows above its capacity and refuses at its connection limit
A validator that catches every wrong answer; a person handling an escalation costs 60 cu

classes.meaning: declared: an assumption the simulation encodes and the article states

items.text: Workload: seeded arrivals, cases and long-tail shapes (seed 4917; E4 calibration seed 1101)
The knowledge fixture (120 documents, 12 queries with declared required evidence ids, a 24-lookup cache sequence) and the 40-case offline eval suite (scripts/make_fixtures.py)

classes.meaning: synthetic inputs generated deterministically and frozen

items.text: A Black Friday surge at 20 requests/s; a finance run of 3,000 items in ten seconds
A payment that never settles (a runaway loop) and a coordinator that re-delegates a failing sub-agent
A 30 s throttle of the EU private deployment
Candidate releases: one tool description, one prompt, one retrieval top-k, one knowledge index, one policy, one routing table; three that break an invariant
The admission bound removed (the negative control)

classes.meaning: a failure or change introduced on purpose

items.text: Autoscaling, real providers' quotas and latency, real prices, real model quality, human approval capacity, shadow traffic, rollback of stateful artifacts (indexes, memory, migrations)

classes.meaning: design this POC does not exercise

rows: Model calls to a real model

provenance.manifest_origin: built by tools/proof_pack.py from ops_poc/runs/2026-10-08-recorded/manifest.json (recorded) and proof/manifest.toml (frozen words)

replay.contract: every file of the run except volatile/ (wall-clock timings) is byte-identical on a rerun from source into a scratch copy

runtime_mode: deterministic discrete-event simulation; scripted agents; simulated providers, tools and clients; no model, no network
scenario: Northwind Goods' shared agent platform on Black Friday (a support surge and a finance reconciliation run on the same slots) and on Cyber Monday (a release that changed no code), simulated deterministically in sim-ms and cost units
source_commit: unknown (not a git repository); source_sha256 lists every POC source file's hash
started_at: unknown (not recorded: a deterministic run records simulated time; wall times live in volatile/)
